fixes.explanation: Matthew doesn't say the crowds were offended. He says, “When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.” (Matthew 22:33). The Sadducees say there is no resurrection (Matthew 22:23), so Jesus tells them they don't know the Scriptures or the power of God. Then He points to God's own words, “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob” and says, “He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” (Matthew 22:32). That's the teaching that left the crowds amazed.

problems.problem: The explanation quotes Jesus’ conclusion but does not explain how His teaching addresses the Sadducees’ denial of the resurrection.
